name: Use measurement language
description: Student can use words like long and short, heavy and light, full and empty, or fast and slow to describe objects and events.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the snake toy is long and the rock is heavy.
commonError: Student uses 'big' for everything, not distinguishing length from mass or capacity.
checkpointTask: Show various objects and events. Ask the student to describe them using measurement words.

name: Compare two objects by length
description: Student can directly compare two objects and say which is longer or shorter.
exampleOfSuccess: Holding two ribbons together at one end, the student says the green one is longer.
commonError: Student compares without lining up the ends.
checkpointTask: Give pairs of objects. Ask the student which is longer, watching whether they line up the ends.

name: Compare two objects by mass
description: Student can directly compare two objects by holding one in each hand and say which is heavier or lighter.
exampleOfSuccess: Holding a book and a feather, the student says the book is heavier.
commonError: Student says the bigger object is always heavier, ignoring what hefting shows.
checkpointTask: Give pairs including a small-heavy and large-light object. Ask which is heavier.

name: Compare the capacity of two containers
description: Student can compare which of two containers holds more.
exampleOfSuccess: Filling one cup and pouring it into another, the student says which holds more.
commonError: Student judges by height alone, assuming taller holds more.
checkpointTask: Give two containers. Ask the student to find which holds more by pouring.

name: Compare the duration of two events
description: Student can start two events at the same time and say which takes longer.
exampleOfSuccess: Starting two timers together, the student says the sand timer finished before the song ended, so the song took longer.
commonError: Student judges by which event they liked more rather than how long it took.
checkpointTask: Start two events together. Ask the student which one takes longer.

name: Name the times of the day
description: Student can name times of the day: morning, lunchtime, afternoon and night.
exampleOfSuccess: The student names morning, lunchtime, afternoon and night when shown pictures of each.
commonError: Student mixes up the times, such as calling a dark sky 'morning'.
checkpointTask: Show pictures of different times of day. Ask the student to name each.

name: Put the times of the day in order
description: Student can sequence the times of the day in order.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders morning, lunchtime, afternoon, night.
commonError: Student orders the pictures by where there is space rather than by time.
checkpointTask: Give pictures of times of day. Ask the student to put them in order.

name: Name the days of the week in order
description: Student can name the days of the week in order.
exampleOfSuccess: The student recites Monday through Sunday in order.
commonError: Student leaves out a day or starts from a different day each time.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to name the days of the week in order.

name: Connect an event to a time of day
description: Student can connect a familiar event to the time of day it usually happens.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says breakfast happens in the morning and bedtime at night.
commonError: Student connects events to the wrong time, or cannot link events to times at all.
checkpointTask: Name familiar events. Ask the student which time of day each usually happens.

name: Tell school days from the weekend
description: Student can tell the difference between school days and the weekend.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says Saturday and Sunday are not school days.
commonError: Student cannot distinguish weekdays from weekend, or names the wrong days.
checkpointTask: Ask the student which days they come to school and which days they do not.
